task.prompt: The course's planar 2R model accepts link lengths 0 < l1, l2 ≤ 10 m and joint angles -2π ≤ q1, q2 ≤ 2π rad (2π ≈ 6.2832). For each input set, choose whether it is inside or outside this domain.
task.solution: Set 1 is inside. Set 2 is outside: l2 = 0 m is not positive. Set 3 is outside: |q1| = 6.5 rad exceeds 2π ≈ 6.2832. Set 4 is inside.
hints: Test four separate conditions for each set: l1 > 0, l2 > 0, both lengths ≤ 10 m, and both |q1|, |q2| ≤ 2π.
Negative joint angles are allowed; only their magnitude is bounded. The bounds include their end points (≤), but a link length of exactly 0 is excluded (<).
Set 1 is inside. Set 2 is outside: l2 = 0 m is not positive. Set 3 is outside: |q1| = 6.5 rad exceeds 2π ≈ 6.2832. Set 4 is inside.
task.remediation: A frequent slip is treating negative joint angles as invalid, rejecting a value exactly on an inclusive bound, or allowing a zero link length. Re-read the input domain stated in the L02-planar kit header (0 < l1, l2 ≤ 10 m, |q| ≤ 2π), then try a fresh practice item before another independent check.

task.prompt: Joint angles are in radians and link lengths in metres. A planar 2R arm has l1 = 1.5 m, l2 = 1.0 m and relative joint angles q1 = 0.5 rad, q2 = 0 rad. Give the tip position x, y in metres. Give 3 decimal places; tolerance ±0.001 m.
task.solution: x = (l1 + l2) cos q1 = 2.5 cos 0.5 = 2.194 m and y = (l1 + l2) sin q1 = 2.5 sin 0.5 = 1.1986 m. In degree mode the same keys give x ≈ 2.4999, y ≈ 0.0218, which treats 0.5 as 0.5° instead of 0.5 rad.
hints: With q2 = 0 both links point the same way, so the arm is a single straight segment of length l1 + l2 at the angle q1.
The straight arm has length 1.5 + 1.0 = 2.5 m along the angle q1 = 0.5 rad; evaluate cos and sin of 0.5 with the calculator in radian mode.
x = (l1 + l2) cos q1 = 2.5 cos 0.5 = 2.194 m and y = (l1 + l2) sin q1 = 2.5 sin 0.5 = 1.1986 m. In degree mode the same keys give x ≈ 2.4999, y ≈ 0.0218, which treats 0.5 as 0.5° instead of 0.5 rad.
task.remediation: If you got x ≈ 2.4999, your calculator was in degree mode; this course always enters joint angles in radians. Set your calculator to radians, revisit /objectives/M01.radians-trig on radian measure, then practise a fresh X11 item before another independent check.

task.prompt: Your function planar_2r(q1, q2, l1, l2) returns the correct x, y and theta of the ideal planar model for every test. For each task below, choose whether that result already establishes it or it needs separate work.

task.solution: Established: tip position and tool orientation for given joint angles (that is the FK map). Needs separate work: inverse kinematics (solving for angles, possibly with several or no solutions) and physical accuracy (calibration, backlash and measurement).
hints: Forward kinematics answers one question: given the joint angles, where is the tool and how is it oriented in the ideal model?
Sort the tasks by direction: angles to pose is FK; pose to angles is the inverse problem. A real robot adds errors that no ideal formula contains.

Established: tip position and tool orientation for given joint angles (that is the FK map). Needs separate work: inverse kinematics (solving for angles, possibly with several or no solutions) and physical accuracy (calibration, backlash and measurement).
task.remediation: A passing FK test is evidence about the forward map of the ideal model only; inverse kinematics and hardware accuracy are separate claims. Re-read what the R04 objective excludes (inverse kinematics, spatial chains, physical accuracy) in /lessons/R04 before another independent check.

task.prompt: Two planar 2R arms both have l1 + l2 = 2.4 m. Arm P has l1 = l2 = 1.2 m; arm Q has l1 = 1.8 m, l2 = 0.6 m. Both use relative joint angles q1 = 0.7 rad and q2 = π/2 rad. Give the base-to-tip distance of each arm in metres. Give 3 decimal places; tolerance ±0.001 m.
task.solution: With cos(π/2) = 0, r = sqrt(l1² + l2²). Arm P: sqrt(1.2² + 1.2²) = 1.6971 m. Arm Q: sqrt(1.8² + 0.6²) = sqrt(3.6) = 1.8974 m. The same total length gives different distances, so unequal links cannot be replaced by their average.
hints: The base-to-tip distance depends on the two link lengths and on q2 only; q1 just rotates the whole arm.
Use r² = l1² + l2² + 2 l1 l2 cos q2 with cos(π/2) = 0, so the elbow forms a right angle; apply it to each arm with its own link lengths.

With cos(π/2) = 0, r = sqrt(l1² + l2²). Arm P: sqrt(1.2² + 1.2²) = 1.6971 m. Arm Q: sqrt(1.8² + 0.6²) = sqrt(3.6) = 1.8974 m. The same total length gives different distances, so unequal links cannot be replaced by their average.
task.remediation: If both distances came out equal, the link lengths were averaged or only their sum was used; FK depends on each length separately. Revisit the reach invariant r² = l1² + l2² + 2 l1 l2 cos q2 in /lessons/R04, then practise a fresh X11 item before another independent check.

task.prompt: Planar 2R arm: l1 = 1.7 m, l2 = 0.9 m; relative joint angles q1 = 0.4 rad, q2 = -1.0 rad (counter-clockwise positive; base at the origin, q1 measured from the +x axis). Compute the tip position x, y and the tool orientation theta (the world angle of link 2) modulo 2π. Give 3 decimal places; tolerance ±0.001 m for x, y and ±0.001 rad for theta.
task.solution: Elbow: (l1 cos q1, l1 sin q1) = (1.7 cos 0.4, 1.7 sin 0.4) = (1.5658, 0.662) m. Link 2 points at the world angle q1 + q2 = 0.4 + (-1.0) = -0.6 rad, so it adds (l2 cos(q1 + q2), l2 sin(q1 + q2)) = (0.7428, -0.5082) m. Tip: x = 1.5658 + 0.7428 = 2.3086 m; y = 0.662 + (-0.5082) = 0.1538 m. theta = q1 + q2 = -0.6 rad (any value that differs by a multiple of 2π is also accepted).
hints: Relative joints: link 1 points at q1 = 0.4 rad from the +x axis, and link 2 points at the world angle q1 + q2, not at q2 = -1.0 rad alone. Keep the calculator in radian mode.
Elbow first: (1.7 cos 0.4, 1.7 sin 0.4) = (1.5658, 0.662) m. Next add a vector of length l2 = 0.9 m pointing at the world angle q1 + q2 = -0.6 rad.

Elbow: (l1 cos q1, l1 sin q1) = (1.7 cos 0.4, 1.7 sin 0.4) = (1.5658, 0.662) m. Link 2 points at the world angle q1 + q2 = 0.4 + (-1.0) = -0.6 rad, so it adds (l2 cos(q1 + q2), l2 sin(q1 + q2)) = (0.7428, -0.5082) m. Tip: x = 1.5658 + 0.7428 = 2.3086 m; y = 0.662 + (-0.5082) = 0.1538 m. theta = q1 + q2 = -0.6 rad (any value that differs by a multiple of 2π is also accepted).
task.remediation: Common slips on this item: treating q2 = -1.0 rad as the world angle of link 2 gives x ≈ 2.0521, y ≈ -0.0953 and theta = -1.0; a calculator in degree mode gives x ≈ 2.5999, y ≈ 0.0024. If your answer matches one of these, the slip is in the angle convention, not the formula. Revisit the relative-angle convention in /lessons/R04, then practise a fresh X11 item before another independent check.

task.prompt: Planar 2R arm: l1 = 1.4 m, l2 = 1.2 m; relative joint angles q1 = 1.9 rad, q2 = 1.6 rad (counter-clockwise positive; base at the origin, q1 measured from the +x axis). Compute the tip position x, y and the tool orientation theta (the world angle of link 2) modulo 2π. Give 3 decimal places; tolerance ±0.001 m for x, y and ±0.001 rad for theta. You may leave theta unwrapped; if you reduce it, use 2π ≈ 6.2832.
task.solution: Elbow: (l1 cos q1, l1 sin q1) = (1.4 cos 1.9, 1.4 sin 1.9) = (-0.452605, 1.32482) m. Link 2 points at the world angle q1 + q2 = 1.9 + 1.6 = 3.5 rad, so it adds (l2 cos(q1 + q2), l2 sin(q1 + q2)) = (-1.123748, -0.42094) m. Tip: x = -0.452605 + (-1.123748) = -1.576353 m; y = 1.32482 + (-0.42094) = 0.90388 m. theta = q1 + q2 = 3.5 rad, which lies outside (-π, π]; subtracting 2π gives 3.5 - 6.2832 = -2.7832 rad. Both 3.5 and -2.7832 are accepted, because orientation is compared modulo 2π.
